gloss: to step down onto; to alight

definitions.gloss: to step down onto; to alight and stand; to descend upon (a place)
definitions.explanation: Compound verb emphasizing the moment of setting foot somewhere, often used for significant arrivals.

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}から{降|お}り{立|た}つと、{暖|あたた}かい{風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}いていた。
examples.english: When I stepped off the plane, a warm wind was blowing.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めて{日本|にほん}の{地|ち}に{降|お}り{立|た}った。
examples.english: I set foot on Japanese soil for the first time.

examples.japanese: {宇宙|うちゅう}{飛行士|ひこうし}が{月|つき}に{降|お}り{立|た}った{瞬間|しゅんかん}は{歴史的|れきしてき}だった。
examples.english: The moment the astronaut stepped onto the moon was historic.

notes:
{降|お}り{立|た}つ is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}) formed from {降|お}りる (to descend) + {立|た}つ (to stand).

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
・[place]に{降|お}り{立|た}つ - to set foot at [place]
・[vehicle]から{降|お}り{立|た}つ - to step down from [vehicle]

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{地|ち}に{降|お}り{立|た}つ - to set foot on the ground
・{空港|くうこう}に{降|お}り{立|た}つ - to arrive at an airport
・{異国|いこく}の{地|ち}に{降|お}り{立|た}つ - to set foot in a foreign land

USAGE:
More literary or dramatic than simple {降|お}りる. Often used for momentous occasions.
